title: A Method for Predicting the Ideal Harmonic-Free Power Spectral Density from the Harmonic Power Spectral Density
content: Based on a 1.8 GHz software-defined radio Universal Software Radio Peripheral (USRP) transmission module and receiving system, this study measures power spectral densities under different transmission gains. It proposes a method to predict the ideal harmonic-free power spectral density from the harmonic power spectral density. The procedure involves: 1) measuring the power spectral density; 2) checking for harmonic peaks, and plotting directly if none are present; 3) calculating equivalent power using different approaches based on the ratio of harmonic peak power to harmonic peak frequency bandwidth; 4) transferring and superimposing the harmonic power onto the main peak of the transmitted wave to form an equivalent power spectral density plot. This method is also applicable to 900 MHz power spectral densities with more complex harmonic signal spectra, effectively obtaining equivalent power. It can predict the equivalent power spectral density under identical transmission gain conditions based on complex harmonic signal spectra. When the power peak exceeds three times the bandwidth, the method simplifies computational complexity by equating the harmonic peak area to a triangular area. This approach holds significant practical value for engineering predictions of equivalent power spectral density.
